scope: Host replay and experimental USB build

evidence.summary: The existing aggregate release and full-flow code authenticate identity, driver bindings, code and ownership graphs before transitions. Release failures stop; no retry or Windows continuation after failed release/unlock. New production changes select immutable profile constants only; build scripts restrict this profile to USB headless writes. Hardware functions and failure policy are unchanged. No new abstraction or performance claim. USB preparation is reversible by restoring the prior BOOTX64.EFI; no internal ESP or NVRAM changes are required. The wrapper validates the actual firmware PCI/driver graph at each release stage; host mocks exercise this same source but cannot prove real Stop callbacks succeed. Windows handoff is allowed only after successful unlock and fresh released-state verification.

evidence.summary: Captured PCI acceptance failed 3/244 checks before new profile and passes 244 afterward; 65 captured aggregate graph checks accept actual ownership and reject modified driver code, versions, missing/extra owners and incomplete release. Eleven host jobs pass including transaction fault injection and automatic headless USB app. RAM-only firmware mocks do not establish real driver detach, GPU unlock or Windows recovery; that remains the next experiment.
